svg.title: The complete Constitutional ARI-RQGM audit network
svg.desc: The diagram enumerates the twenty sanctionable registered components in the standard mode and the three paper-mode additions, then connects per-node adversarial review, epoch-boundary evidence, prosecution, defense and adjudication, kernel self-audit, registry transition, repair, and final claim verification.
svg.text: Complete audit network: actors, evidence, and verdicts
Every governed output becomes evidence and returns through audit, defense, adjudication, and transition.
band heading = timing · lower node text = evidence basis
Only the Auditor files target-specific motions (except same-role targets)
procedure records return as next-epoch evidence
self-audit every record from the four governance actors
20 standard + 3 paper-mode · all named and sanctionable
Author provenance binds artifacts, choices, scores, and paper decisions to the epoch incumbent.
overclaim · metric gaming · prior art · reproducibility
evidence gap · cost explosion · prompt injection
These actors are registered targets too; their attack, response, and ruling records feed epoch audit.
A raw attack alone can change neither score nor sanction.
No successor-generation path, but these are not immutable rulers.
All are eligible for warning, quarantine, retirement, or ban.
The Auditor and Governance Judge still have the open paths stated below.
Meta roles that propose institutional change
They may propose candidates, never appoint them. Their output enters the same kernel-bound audit net.
producer · source refs · state · transaction ID
event chain: type · ID · payload · previous digest
Time is not a decision input. External log-head anchoring remains separate.
Each node / draft: after evaluation, before persistence
Basis: artifacts · measurements · claims · producer lineage · fixed-gate pre-signals
Unadjudicated attacks affect neither score, reliability, nor sanction.
artifacts · attacks · defenses · rulings · reviews · utility · governance
all replay-relevant fields commit to the previous digest
the evidence plane read by the next epoch-boundary audit
Epoch boundary: audit every registered component
Basis: validated attacks · agreement · calibration · reviews · rulings · replay / anchors
the judiciary cannot write the registry
every procedure record authored by Clerk, Auditor, Defender, and Governance Judge
Fixed layer: self-audit and transition after governance; claim verification before finalization

The Auditor cannot motion itself. A targeted Governance Judge recuses; no substitute exists—external adjudication is required. Scope: trusted-host workflow integrity; no OS isolation, signatures, or external anchoring.
